title: A Google Calendar event claims a PR shipped that isn't merged
author: nisaba
description: The Calendar-side twin of mention-claims-unmerged-pr (the X-mention leg), slack-message-claims-unmerged-pr (the Slack-channel leg), linear-comment-claims-unmerged-pr (the Linear-comment leg), and the second leg calendar-event-claims-unfixed-issue (task 1258, the hundred-second real recipe) opened for the Calendar toolkit's own claims-X grid. That recipe's closing-keyword check watches a claim against the issue tracker; this one watches a ships/includes/merges/via claim against the PR tracker -- the two targets are separate GitHub number spaces and separate claim grammars, so one recipe's clean bill never speaks for the other's. Extracts every real 'ships #N'/'includes #N'/'merges #N'/'via #N' claim phrase (seam_engine.pr_claims' shared grammar, imported verbatim) from a calendar event's own title+description and cross-checks it against the live PR tracker's own state. A PR that exists but is not merged is the seam: an event already sitting on a connected calendar disagrees with GitHub's own record, and nothing on either platform ever compares them. Fixture-only, MOCK ONLY, never a live network call -- zero Google Calendar tools are exposed on the-hand gateway today, the same WIP note calendar-event-claims-unfixed-issue already carries. Neither scope is new (ListEvents and ListPullRequests are both already cleared on SCOPES.md's oath table) and google_calendar+github is not a new toolkit pair (calendar-event-claims-unfixed-issue and milestone-deadline-no-calendar-event both already propose it).
confidence_notes: Age-gated off the event's own start time, holding calendar-event-claims-unfixed-issue's own 0.85/0.5 bar exactly -- not an independently re-reasoned number just because the target changed from an issue to a PR. A calendar event is posted once (created) and stands, the same 'posted once and stands' reasoning every claims-unmerged-pr sibling already gives for its own identical bar (not review-comment-claims-unmerged-pr's lower 0.55/0.85 bar, which exists only because a review comment is an editable surface). A claim checked within 24 hours of the event's own start might still be a race (the real merge landing moments after the meeting) rather than a settled overclaim (0.5, below the 0.70 confidence bar, shown as a weighed-and-dropped coincidence, not hidden). At or past 24 hours with the named PR still unmerged, it is unambiguous (flat 0.85). The check itself is objective: the claimed PR's own live merged/state fields, verified against ListPullRequests, not a guess about which tracker the organizer meant. A named PR that does not exist at all is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- a broken reference is a future calendar-side dangling-reference recipe's own seam, not this one's. A named PR that IS merged is excluded too -- the claim was simply true. An event with no ships/includes/merges/via claim phrase at all produces no candidate. No text in this recipe's own headline/detail strings ever names or grades the organizer -- CONTRIBUTING.md's 'No grading, ever' law, same as every recipe in this engine.
